questions.0.explain.t: The audit trail is the basis for detecting abuse and investigating incidents.

questions.0.options.0.t: Recording API calls: who did what, when and from where

questions.0.options.1.t: Blocking malicious traffic before it reaches the application

questions.0.options.2.t: Encrypting data at rest in the storage services

questions.0.options.3.t: Scaling the infrastructure according to the applications' load

questions.0.q.t: What is the role of CloudTrail (or similar)?

questions.1.explain.t: The first thing many attackers do is try to turn off or delete the logs.

questions.1.options.0.t: So an attacker with access to the production account cannot erase their tracks

questions.1.options.1.t: To save storage in the production accounts

questions.1.options.2.t: To speed up the queries made by the security team

questions.1.options.3.t: Because the law requires logs to be kept in two different accounts

questions.1.q.t: Why send logs to a separate, immutable account?

questions.2.explain.t: Too many alerts become fatigue; with no owner or action, nobody responds.

questions.2.options.0.t: Being actionable: saying what happened, where and what to do, with low noise

questions.2.options.1.t: Firing on every event, so that no occurrence goes unnoticed

questions.2.options.2.t: Being sent in a weekly email that summarizes all the events

questions.2.options.3.t: Having no defined owner, so that anyone can act
